notesStmt.note: This page was likely sent to the Ferguson Brothers, the printers of Good-Bye My Fancy, sometime between April 7 and April 11, 1891. It was therefore likely composed in the days and weeks prior to that, in the early months of 1891.

These pages are the copy text for the essay "America's Bulk Average" that Whitman sent to the printer to be set in type and printed as galley proofs for Good-Bye My Fancy (1891). Whitman had previously sent to the printer the copy for the opening poetry section and the majority of the prose section of the volume (see loc.04417 and loc.08498, respectively). He sent the copy for the final prose pieces over the following two months.

body.head: America's ‸summ'd bulk average caps head
body.p: If I were asked ‸persona to the specify the one point of America's people on which I mainly rely, I should say the ‸final average or bulk quality of the whole.

¶ Happy indeed w'd I consider myself to give a fair reflection and representation of even a portion of times, shows, questions, humanity, events, ‸unfoldings, thoughts, &c. &c. my times age in America. these States. ¶ The great social, political, historic function of ‸all my time has been of course the Secession War.—‸¶ ¶ And was out of its multiform considerations and results unfolding one after another ‸along through the centuries ‸now here to give a passing glance at ‸ one.

Was there not something grand after all, and an inside proof of ‸perennial grandeur in ‸the secession war of 1862, '3 and '4 that war? that war! We talk of our own ages and the States' materialism—and it is too true. But how, amid all the ‸whole sordidness—the entire devotion of America, at any price to mere pecuniary success, merchandize—of disregarding all but business and profit—this war, for bare idea and abstraction, a mere, ‸at bottom heroic dream and reminiscence, burst forth in its great devouring flame and conflagration quickly and fiercely spreading and raging, and enveloping all, defining in two marked conflicting ideas—first the Union cause—second the other, a strange deadly interrogation point, hard to define—what—can we not now safely confess it? with magnificent rays, streaks of noblest heroism, fortitude, perseverance, and even conscientiousness, through its pervadingly malignant darkness.

What an area and rounded field, upon the whole—the spirit, arrogance, grim tenacity of the south—the long stretches of murky gloom—the ‸general National Will below and behind ‸and comprehending all—not once ‸really wavering, not a day, not an hour—what could be, or ever can be, grander?

As in this that war, its four years—as through all the ‸whole history and development of the New World—these States through all trials, processes, eruptions, deepest dilemmas, (often straining, tugging at society's heart⹀strings, as if some divine curiosity would find out how much this democracy could stand,) have so far finally and, ‸for more than a century, best justified themselves to profound examination by the average impalpable quality and personality of the bulk, the People en⹀masse.
... I am not sure but my main and chief however indefinite claim for all or any page of mine w'd be its derivation, ‸or, seeking to derive itself, f'm that average quality of the American bulk, the people, and getting back or seeking to get back, to it again.
